chunks.title: SecureVault AI — problem & solution
chunks.text:
Project: SecureVault AI (Security Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Solution: Encrypt files on the user's own device so they never leave it, and pair that with automated threat scanning, passwordless biometric login and auditable key storage.

chunks.title: SecureVault AI — features
chunks.text:
Project: SecureVault AI (Security Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Features:
- AES-256-GCM file encryption with PBKDF2 key derivation (310k iterations)
- Random salt & IV per file; batch file processing; 100% local — files never leave your device
- AI threat scanner: Shannon entropy analysis, file-signature matching, confidence scoring
- VirusTotal API integration
- Biometric authentication via WebAuthn (fingerprint / platform authenticators) — zero biometric data stored
- Blockchain key vault on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet with MetaMask, immutable audit trail and key revocation
- Zero-knowledge sharing: password never in the share URL, expiring links, max view count, one-click revocation, checksum verification
- Security analytics: real-time security score, threat history charts, event audit log, risk dashboard

chunks.title: SecureVault AI — architecture
chunks.text:
Project: SecureVault AI (Security Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Architecture components:
- User (client): Signs in with a password or a WebAuthn platform authenticator (fingerprint / face). No biometric data is stored by the app.
- React + Vite app (frontend): Single-page app built with React 18 and Vite 5, deployed on Vercel. Hosts the dashboard, scanner, vault and sharing UI.
- Encryption engine (ai): AES-256-GCM with keys derived through PBKDF2 (310k iterations) and a random salt + IV per file. Runs locally, so files never leave the device.
- AI threat scanner (ai): Analyses files with Shannon entropy and signature matching, produces a confidence score, and can cross-check with the VirusTotal API.
- Serverless API (api): The repository contains an api/ directory alongside the Vercel config. Its exact responsibilities are not documented yet.
- Blockchain key vault (data): Key records are stored on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet through MetaMask, giving an immutable audit trail with support for key revocation.
- VirusTotal (external): External threat-intelligence service used by the scanner for additional verification.
Data flow: user → frontend; frontend → crypto; frontend → scanner; frontend → api; scanner → virustotal; frontend → chain.

chunks.title: Stock Price Prediction — problem & solution
chunks.text:
Project: Stock Price Prediction (AI Lab). Status: Completed — Finished project with public source code.
Problem: Investors want to know where the market is heading, but forecasting stock prices is notoriously hard.
Solution: Predict the next-day return from engineered price features, compare against naive and drift baselines, and check statistical significance and a simple trading simulation before trusting any model.

chunks.title: Stock Price Prediction — features
chunks.text:
Project: Stock Price Prediction (AI Lab). Status: Completed — Finished project with public source code.
Features:
- Exploratory analysis: trends, return distribution, volatility, correlations and autocorrelation
- 20 engineered features: lagged returns, moving-average gaps, momentum, volatility, RSI and S&P 500 returns
- Chronological split: train 70% (2007–2013), validation 15%, test 15% (Oct 2014 – Feb 2016)
- Models: Naive and Drift baselines, Ridge Regression, Random Forest and an LSTM (Keras)
- Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE, R², directional accuracy, a binomial significance test and a trading simulation

chunks.title: NEXA — architecture

Project: NEXA (AI Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Architecture components:
- NEXA website (frontend): Static chat site on GitHub Pages (and the NEXA panel in this portfolio). Talks only to the NEXA API; falls back to in-browser BM25 documentation search.
- NEXA API (api): FastAPI service in Docker on Render. Validates input, enforces CORS and rate limits, and exposes /health and /chat.
- Retrieval (ai): BM25 with title boosting, synonym expansion and project focus. Always adds a project's 'not yet documented' note so gaps can be cited.
- Knowledge base (data): Chunks generated from projects.js, profile.js and each project's GitHub README, published by the portfolio and loaded at startup.
- LLM (external): Writes the answer from the retrieved chunks only, returning JSON with the ids it cited; the API keeps only ids it actually retrieved.
Data flow: ui → api; api → rag; rag → kb; rag → llm.

chunks.title: MindScape AI — architecture
chunks.text:
Project: MindScape AI (Knowledge Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Architecture components:
- Notes app (frontend): Editor, note list, connections panel, graph and Ask views. Static site on GitHub Pages.
- Embedding worker (ai): Web Worker running all-MiniLM-L6-v2 with Transformers.js, so typing never stutters.
- Similarity engine (ai): Cosine similarity for related notes, search and graph links; TF-IDF fallback; passage chunking for Ask.
- IndexedDB (data): Notes and cached embeddings, stored only in this browser.
- Model files (external): The ~23 MB model downloads once from Hugging Face and is cached by the browser.
Data flow: ui → worker; worker → hub; ui → sim; ui → db; sim → db.

chunks.title: MindScape AI — challenges
chunks.text:
Project: MindScape AI (Knowledge Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Challenges:
- A new note waited for its database write before opening, so fast typing was overwritten; it now opens first and saves in the background
- Embedding similarity and TF-IDF overlap run in different ranges, so thresholds are tuned per engine
- The model is ~23 MB, so it loads in a Web Worker while the app works in keyword mode

chunks.title: EarthPulse — problem & solution
chunks.text:
Project: EarthPulse (Earth Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Problem: Earth data is scattered across agencies and formats, so seeing what's happening now, and how a place's climate has changed, takes several sites.
Solution: One map pulls live feeds from USGS, NASA EONET and Open-Meteo directly in the browser, and turns any clicked point into weather, air quality and warming stripes.

- Open-Meteo (external): Forecast, air-quality, geocoding and ERA5 archive APIs.

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — problem & solution
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI (Bio Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Problem: Spotting plant disease early, or knowing how to care for a plant you can't name, usually means asking an expert.
Solution: Run two image classifiers in the browser, rate how much each result can be trusted, and pair it with care guidance and a leaf-colour check.

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — features
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI (Bio Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Features:
- Crop health: 38 healthy and diseased classes across 14 crops, with cause, signs and what to do
- House plants: 47 species with light, water and pet-toxicity notes (ASPCA listings)
- Calibrated High / Moderate / Low confidence, with alternatives and photo tips when unsure
- Leaf-aware colour check that ignores pots, soil and skin, with a discoloured-area overlay
- Upload, drag and drop, paste, phone camera or sample photos; photos never leave the device

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — challenges
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI (Bio Lab). Status: Live — Shipped and publicly available.
Challenges:
- The int8 disease model uses an operator (ConvInteger) that the browser runtime doesn't support, so the app uses the 9 MB fp32 build
- The house-plant model spreads its scores thinly (~13% for correct answers), so confidence is judged by the margin over the runner-up
- Pots, skin and sunlit leaves skewed the colour check, so discolouration now only counts inside leaf tissue, with recalibrated hue bands

# NEXA
**An AI assistant that answers questions about my work, and only from my documented work.**
💬 **Live site:** https://nausheen1295.github.io/nexa/
NEXA answers questions about my projects, skills and experience, in the style you need: recruiter, developer, simple, architecture or interview. It uses retrieval-augmented generation over my portfolio's documentation, cites its sources, and says so when something isn't documented instead of guessing.
Part of the AI Lab in my portfolio, [NEXUS](https://nausheen1295.github.io/portfolio/), where NEXA also has its own panel.

chunks.title: NEXA — README: Two ways it answers
chunks.text:
Project: NEXA. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## Two ways it answers
| | Documentation search (works now) | AI answers (once the API is hosted) |
|---|---|---|
| How | BM25 search in the browser over the knowledge base | NEXA API: retrieval → LLM → citation check |
| Output | The best-matching passages, with links | A written answer in the chosen mode, with verified sources |
| Never | Imitates AI | Cites a document it didn't retrieve |

chunks.title: MindScape AI — README: MindScape AI
chunks.text:
Project: MindScape AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
# MindScape AI
**A private, AI-powered second brain.** Write notes and MindScape links related ideas, maps your knowledge as a graph and answers questions from what you've written.
🧠 **Live site:** https://nausheen1295.github.io/mindscape-ai/
The AI runs **on your device**. Notes are stored in your browser and never sent to a server.
Part of the Knowledge Lab in my portfolio, [NEXUS](https://nausheen1295.github.io/portfolio/).

chunks.title: MindScape AI — README: Features
chunks.text:
Project: MindScape AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## Features
- **Notes:**
  - Markdown with a live preview.
  - Tag with `#tag` and link with `[[Note title]]`; clicking a link to a note that doesn't exist yet creates it.
  - Notes autosave, and you can download any note as a `.md` file.
- **Related by meaning:** every note is turned into a 384-dimension sentence embedding.
  - MindScape lists the notes closest in meaning, even with no words in common (e.g. *AES-GCM* ↔ *Password hashing*).
  - One click links a related note into the one you're writing.
- **Semantic search:** search "keeping my secrets safe" and you get the security notes. Results are ranked by a blend of meaning and keywords.
- **Knowledge graph:** an interactive force-directed map.
  - Solid lines are your links, and dashed lines are connections found by meaning, with an adjustable similarity threshold.
  - Drag, zoom, hover to highlight neighbours, and click to open a note. It also works with the keyboard.
- **Ask your notes:** ask a question in plain words.
  - Every passage in your notebook is scored against the question, and the best matches are shown with their source note.
  - It is extractive: MindScape never writes text that isn't in your notes, and it says so when nothing matches.
- **Tags, links and backlinks:** filter by tag, and see which notes link here.
- **Backups:** export and import JSON, add the sample notes, or start empty.
- **Fallback:** keyword (TF-IDF) matching is used until the model loads, or if it can't.

chunks.title: MindScape AI — README: How it works
chunks.text:
Project: MindScape AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## How it works
```
Notes (IndexedDB, this browser only)
   │
   ├── js/semantic.js        parse [[links]] / #tags, TF-IDF fallback, cosine similarity,
   │                         semantic link selection, passage chunking   (unit-tested)
   ├── js/embed-worker.js    Web Worker running all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (quantised ONNX, ~23 MB)
   │                         via Transformers.js; mean-pooled, L2-normalised embeddings
   ├── js/store.js           IndexedDB: notes + embedding cache keyed by content hash
   └── js/app.js             editor, related notes, search, D3 force graph, Ask
```
- **Off the main thread:** the model runs in a Web Worker, so typing never stutters. It downloads once and is then cached by the browser.
- **Embedding cache:** embeddings are cached by a hash of each note's text, so only notes that change are re-embedded.
- **Link selection:** each note keeps at most its strongest few semantic partners, so a general note can't link to everything.

Project: InsightForge. Status: Live. Source: project README.
# InsightForge
**Drop in a dataset and get the story.** Automatic profiling, recommended charts and plain-language insights.
📊 **Live site:** https://nausheen1295.github.io/insightforge/
InsightForge turns a raw CSV into answers in seconds. It works out what each column is, measures it, picks the charts that suit the data, and writes up what stands out, with the numbers behind every finding. Everything runs in your browser tab, so your file is never uploaded.
Part of the Data Lab in my portfolio, [NEXUS](https://nausheen1295.github.io/portfolio/).

chunks.title: InsightForge — README: Features
chunks.text:
Project: InsightForge. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## Features
- **Load anything tabular:** CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, or JSON arrays.
  - Drag and drop, choose a file, or paste data. Files can be up to 50 MB (200,000 rows).
- **Automatic profiling:** each column is classified as number, category, date, yes/no, ID or text.
  - Shows missing values, distinct counts, mean, median, standard deviation, range and outliers (1.5 × IQR).
  - Each column also gets a mini histogram or its top values.
- **Plain-language insights,** ranked by strength:
  - trends over time (start vs end, peak)
  - strong correlations (Pearson r)
  - which category explains the most variation in a measure (η²)
  - skewed distributions, outliers, dominant categories
  - data-quality issues: gaps, duplicate rows, constant columns
  - Every finding shows its evidence, and none claims cause and effect.
- **Recommended charts:**
  - a line chart for date columns, plus several measures indexed to 100 so they compare on one axis
  - a scatter plot of the strongest relationship, coloured by group
  - average by the most influential category, category counts, and histograms
- **Chart builder:** bar, line, scatter or histogram, with count, sum, mean, median, min or max and colour-by. It explains why when a combination doesn't make sense.
- **Correlation heatmap** across numeric columns.
- **Data table** with filtering and sorting.
- **Downloadable report:** a Markdown summary of findings and column profiles.
- **Accessible charts:** every chart has a table view, and colour palettes are colour-blind-checked in both light and dark themes.

chunks.title: InsightForge — README: How it works
chunks.text:
Project: InsightForge. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## How it works
```
File / paste / sample
      │  PapaParse (delimiter sniffing) or JSON.parse
      ▼
js/profile.js   pure analysis engine (unit-tested)
      │  type inference → column stats → correlations, η², skew, outliers, trends
      ├──► insights()      ranked plain-language findings with evidence
      └──► suggestCharts() chart specs chosen from column types and relationships
      ▼
js/charts.js    Chart.js rendering; colours read from CSS tokens per theme
js/app.js       tabs, builder, columns, heatmap, table, report export
```
- **Rule-based insights:** findings come from a statistical engine, not a language model. That makes them fast, private and reproducible, and every sentence can be traced to a number.
- **Type inference:** detection is tolerant of currency symbols, thousands separators, percentages, common "missing" markers (`NA`, `null`, `-`, …) and several date formats.
- **Large files:** long series are evenly thinned for drawing, but all statistics use every row.

Project: EarthPulse. Status: Live. Source: project README.
# EarthPulse
**Climate & geospatial intelligence on one live map.**
🌍 **Live site:** https://nausheen1295.github.io/earthpulse/
EarthPulse brings real-time earth data together in one place. See earthquakes and natural events as they happen, then click any point on the planet to get its weather, air quality and long-term climate trend.
Part of the Earth Lab in my portfolio, [NEXUS](https://nausheen1295.github.io/portfolio/).

chunks.title: EarthPulse — README: Features
chunks.text:
Project: EarthPulse. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## Features
- **Live earthquakes:** USGS feeds for the past day, week or month.
  - Marker size shows magnitude and colour shows depth.
  - Tsunami flags are shown, and every quake links to its USGS event page.
- **Natural events:** open NASA EONET events (wildfires, severe storms, volcanoes, sea ice and more), filterable by type.
- **Any place on Earth:** click the map, search a city or use your location to see:
  - current weather and a 7-day forecast
  - air quality (US AQI, PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂)
  - the climate trend since 1950
- **Climate trend:**
  - Warming stripes and a yearly anomaly chart against the 1991–2020 average, built from ERA5 reanalysis.
  - Also shows the trend in °C per decade, how the past 12 months compare, and the warmest year on record for that point.
- **Shareable links:** the selected place is kept in the URL (`?lat=…&lon=…&name=…`).
- **Auto-refresh:** feeds refresh every 5 minutes.
- **Themes and devices:** dark and light themes, keyboard-friendly tabs and search, and a layout that works on phones.

chunks.title: EarthPulse — README: How it works
chunks.text:
Project: EarthPulse. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## How it works
```
Browser (static site on GitHub Pages)
│
├── Leaflet map ◄── OpenStreetMap tiles
├── js/api.js ──► USGS earthquake GeoJSON feeds
│             ──► NASA EONET v3 events
│             ──► Open-Meteo forecast, air-quality, geocoding and ERA5 archive APIs
│             ──► Nominatim reverse geocoding (place names for clicked points)
├── js/climate.js   pure functions: yearly anomalies, trend, 12-month anomaly, colour scales
└── js/app.js       map layers, panels, search and URL state
```
- There is no backend and no API keys. Every data source is free, public and allows browser requests.
- The climate maths runs in the browser on about 27,000 daily values per place.
- Only complete years count, so a partial year never looks unusually warm or cold.
- Each panel fails on its own. If one source is down, the rest of the page keeps working, and a newer selection always replaces an older one that is still loading.

# FloraMind AI
**Computer-vision plant intelligence that runs on your device.** Snap a leaf to check it for common crop diseases, or identify a house plant and get care and pet-safety notes.
🌿 **Live site:** https://nausheen1295.github.io/floramind-ai/
Photos are never uploaded: both neural networks run in the browser with Transformers.js.
Part of the Bio Lab in my portfolio, [NEXUS](https://nausheen1295.github.io/portfolio/).

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — README: Features
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## Features
- **Check crop health:**
  - 38 classes covering 14 crops (tomato, potato, apple, grape, maize, pepper, peach, strawberry and more), both healthy and diseased.
  - Each diagnosis comes with its cause, what to look for, and what you can do.
- **Identify a house plant:** 47 popular indoor plants, with light and water needs and pet toxicity based on ASPCA listings. Highly toxic plants such as lilies and sago palm are flagged.
- **Leaf colour check:**
  - Measures green, yellow and brown leaf tissue, ignoring pots, soil, skin and background.
  - Can highlight discoloured areas on the photo.
  - Clearly labelled as an *indicator*, not a diagnosis.
- **Honest confidence:**
  - Every result is rated High, Moderate or Low, with alternatives listed.
  - Low-confidence results say so, and give tips for a better photo instead of guessing.
- **Input options:** upload, drag and drop, paste, phone camera, or six sample photos.

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — README: How it works
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
## How it works
```
Photo ─► canvas (≤ 900 px) ─┬─► js/analysis.js      leaf-aware colour classification (unit-tested)
                            │
                            └─► js/vision-worker.js  Web Worker + Transformers.js (ONNX Runtime Web)
                                   ├─ crop health: MobileNet-v2, fine-tuned on New Plant Diseases (38 classes, 9 MB)
                                   └─ house plants: ViT-Base, fine-tuned on 47 house plants (4-bit, ~57 MB, loaded on demand)
                                         │ top-5 labels + scores
                                         ▼
                            rateResult() confidence tiers ─► js/care.js guidance ─► result card
```

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — README: Confidence calibration
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
### Confidence calibration
The two models behave very differently, so each gets its own rule. I tested them on openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photos before setting the thresholds.
| Model | Behaviour on real photos | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Crop health | Sharp: correct answers often score 35–98% | High ≥ 60% · Moderate ≥ 30% and 1.5× the runner-up |
| House plants | Flat: correct answers score ~13% against ~3% for the next guess | High: ≥ 2.5× the runner-up · Moderate ≥ 1.6× |

chunks.title: FloraMind AI — README: Field test
chunks.text:
Project: FloraMind AI. Status: Live. Source: project README.
### Field test
The lab results don't carry over fully to real-world photos:
| Model | Reported accuracy (own test set) | My test on Wikimedia Commons photos |
|---|---|---|
| Crop health | ~95% | 10 of 25 exactly right (crop + disease), 12 of 25 right disease. It was right on all 6 tomato Septoria photos and often mixed up potato and tomato late blight. Several test images were microscope shots or drawings. |
| House plants | ~90% | 16 of 23 right (top answer) |
The crop model was trained on PlantVillage-style photos: single leaves on plain backgrounds. It does best on similar shots, which is why the app asks for one leaf filling the frame.
